title_chain.zh_h1: 莫利纽克斯问题 Molyneux’s problem (Brian Glenney, Gabriele Ferretti, and Marjolein Degenaar)

spot.html_text: New accounts of different kinds of blind subjects, most of whom could distinguish light from dark but not shapes, in a variety of different experimental conditions, suggested that, after time, some newly sighted subjects could partially distinguish and identify visual properties by sight alone. (Abbott 1864) Sir Everard Home (1807) tested a young boy age 10, about the distances of candlelight and the sun, giving a report similar to Cheselden’s boy saying, “it appeared to touch his eyes.” (Abbott
